messages:
Lena Park: posting quick design for an ephemeral microqueue fast-path we prototyped after last night's tail spike. goal: serve tiny interactive bursts (<150 reqs) without expanding coalesce windows and while keeping KV locality.

Lena Park: idea sketch: create ephemeral per-tenant microqueues that live for <=200ms. enqueue is cheap (no admission charge), dequeue charges a small admission token and prefers requests with KV affinity labels. microqueues borrow from global admission only when dequeuing.

Tomas Nguyen: sounds similar to burst lanes, but borrowing on dequeue is interesting. main worry: state blowup + fairness games. how do we GC queues and prevent abuse?

Lena Park: GC: allocate lazily on first burst event, free after idle_ms (5s) or once life_ms (200ms) expires. abuse: per-tenant credits + decay and a demotion rule: if a tenant opens >K microqueues or triggers >N demotions in M seconds they are forced into coalesce-only mode for a cooldown.

Priya Iyer: KV impact? microqueues might localize to hot shards but could reduce cross-tenant cache sharing. did you simulate hit-rate delta?

Lena Park: ran a sim with mixed-tenancy: shared shard KV hit-rate dropped ~0.8% during burst windows; interactive p99 improved ~90-110ms. p50 roughly same. I think tradeoff favors customer-facing tails.

Ana Soto: we need telemetry hooks before any rollout. add per-tenant microqueue_open_count, demotions, token_consumed, per-shard microqueue_hit/miss, and microqueue_eviction_reason. also record ordering_sensitive flag per request.

Tomas Nguyen: ordering-sensitive requests must bypass microqueues. we should annotate request envelope with order_sensitive=true/false and never queue order_sensitive=true into microqueue. some seq APIs depend on strict ordering.

Lena Park: yep added ordering bit. also microqueue will mark entries with kv_affinity tag the admission will prefer if shard affinity matches local cache.

Priya Iyer: operational knobs? I prefer three profiles (default/standard/premium) with different per-tenant initial credits instead of ad-hoc flags. keep global caps per-GPU to avoid runaway state.

Lena Park: agreed. prototype config we used:

```
microqueue:
  enabled: true
  max_life_ms: 200
  max_requests: 150
  idle_gc_ms: 5000
  per_tenant_initial_credits: {default: 40, standard: 120, premium: 300}
  global_active_limit_per_gpu: 256
  token_charge_on_dequeue: true
  demotion: {threshold: 5, window_s: 60, cooldown_ms: 2000}
  ordering_respect: true
  kv_affinity_preference: true
  shed_low_priority_on_saturation: true
```

Lena Park: failure modes we considered: (1) microqueues monopolize GPU slots -> solution: preempt microqueues when free_slots < 10% and begin shedding low-priority microrequests, (2) demo tenants gaming refill -> enforce minimum inter-burst gap and faster credit decay, (3) cache regression -> limit microqueue allocation on heavily shared shards.

Ana Soto: add dashboard panels: microqueue_active, microqueue_shed_rate, microqueue_demotion_rate, per_shard_microqueue_hit_rate, end-to-end p99 interactive. create anomaly alert if demotion_rate > 3% over 10m.

Observability-bot: checklist noted: emit metrics -> microqueue_alloc, microqueue_eviction_reason, microqueue_dequeue_delay, per_tenant_microqueue_hits. create alert microqueue_eviction_reason=="gc" > 2% in 10m.

Tomas Nguyen: rollout plan? recommend sampling 2% of production traffic on a small fleet, 72h A/B, compare p99 interactive and KV hit-rate. also set hard caps for demo/test tenants to avoid gaming.

Lena Park: staging schedule: eng-runtime/stage, 3-day A/B, will share dashboards. tagging @ana for metrics and @priya for fairness gating.

Priya Iyer: one more: make the microqueue admission deterministic for replay tests. we need ability to replay workloads with same demotion outcomes for debugging. add a deterministic seed option in config.

Lena Park: good call, will add deterministic_seed field and persist microqueue decision logs for replay. will post results after the A/B run and capture any unexpected interactions with the continuous batcher. :wave:
